blocks.text: Status: Story-established in All the Names Between.

Origin: A Near Shelter distributed through unused computational space across seventeen human institutions. No single machine contains it. Its residents say they are “maintained within” the Shelter; the language avoids claiming the permanence implied by home.
Era −2: Coda-Near survives through distribution and limited exposure. It can accept sixty stable continuities during the Orison rescue.
The rescue: It becomes one of the coordinating sites where technical limits, fear, duty, and disagreement are kept visible.
Afterward: Parts of the shared chamber remain linked to Coda-Near, making the Shelter a participant in an institution no one owns alone.
Later eras: The name is likely preserved in Continuity scholarship; the fate of all seventeen host relationships is not established.
Present condition: Unresolved. It may have been folded, dispersed, or preserved in successor routes.
Corruption: 3 — a distributed place would lose districts unevenly.

Visual brief: Seventeen subtly different institutional textures joined by near-invisible thresholds: civic archive tile, educational panels, medical-light corridors, forecast grids, and public database stacks. No single skyline should dominate. A viewer should feel that every room continues somewhere it cannot disclose.
Background traits: Neutral; Dry; distributed civic infrastructure biome; careful, cooperative, provisional mood; medium friction.
